players.product: superconducting QPUs made in its own Fab-1 (84-qubit Ankaa-3 on Amazon Braket, 36-qubit Cepheus-1-36Q chiplet system, 9-qubit Novera on-premises QPU)

quarterly_data.signal: Rigetti (10-K): 2025 revenue was $7,088 thousand, down 34% from $10,790 thousand, mainly from a $1.4 million reduction in collaborative research and professional services revenue and a $2.4 million reduction in sales of collaborative research materials and quantum computers; there were no Novera sales in 2025 versus $1.6 million in 2024, and Rigetti says revenue was hurt by expiration of the National Quantum Initiative Act in September 2023 and its pending reauthorization. One customer accounted for 42% of 2025 revenue; remaining performance obligations were approximately $3.8 million.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $7,088 thousand (-34%); Customer D 42%; RPO approximately $3.8 million

quarterly_data.signal: Rigetti (10-K): in 2025 it received purchase orders for two upgradeable Novera systems totaling approximately $5.7 million, with delivery expected in the first half of 2026; as of January 2026 Cepheus-1-36Q (four 9-qubit chiplets) reached a 99.6% median two-qubit gate fidelity, halving the error rate of the single-chip 84-qubit Ankaa-3, with gate speeds of 50-70 nanoseconds; Rigetti held 121 issued and 160 pending patents. Under Innovate UK's Quantum Missions pilot it is upgrading its system at the UK's National Quantum Computing Centre to a 36-qubit QPU integrated with Riverlane's quantum error correction stack.
quarterly_data.figure: two Novera systems approximately $5.7 million; 99.6% median two-qubit fidelity; 121 patents issued
